obligations.summary: Deployers of high-risk AI systems must take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure use in accordance with the instructions for use accompanying the systems.
Deployers must assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training, authority, and support.
Deployers who exercise control over input data must ensure that input data is relevant and sufficiently representative in view of the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.
exceptions: Obligation only applies to the extent the deployer exercises control over the input data.

obligations.summary: Deployers must monitor the operation of the high-risk AI system based on instructions for use, inform providers per Article 72 where relevant, and without undue delay notify the provider or distributor and the relevant market surveillance authority and suspend use if the system presents a risk; deployers must also immediately inform the provider and then importer or distributor and market surveillance authorities of any serious incident.
exceptions: The monitoring obligation does not cover sensitive operational data of deployers that are law enforcement authorities.
Deployers that are financial institutions subject to Union financial services law internal governance requirements fulfil the monitoring obligation by complying with those rules.

obligations.summary: Deployers must retain the logs automatically generated by high-risk AI systems, to the extent those logs are under their control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose but at least six months.
exceptions: The six-month minimum period does not apply where applicable Union or national law, in particular Union law on the protection of personal data, provides otherwise.

Deployers that are financial institutions subject to Union financial services law internal governance requirements shall maintain logs as part of documentation kept pursuant to the relevant Union financial service law.

obligations.summary: Deployers who are employers must inform workers' representatives and affected workers before putting into service or using a high-risk AI system at the workplace that they will be subject to its use.
exceptions: Information must be provided in accordance with applicable Union and national law and practice on worker information where such rules apply.

obligations.summary: Deployers that are public authorities or Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies must comply with registration obligations under Article 49, and must not use a high-risk AI system that has not been registered in the EU database referred to in Article 71, informing the provider or distributor if this is the case.

Deployers of high-risk AI systems must, where applicable, use the information provided under Article 13 to comply with their obligation to carry out a data protection impact assessment under Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or Article 27 of Directive (EU) 2016/680.

Deployers of high-risk AI systems for post-remote biometric identification used in a criminal investigation must obtain prior or prompt (within 48 hours) authorisation from a judicial or binding administrative authority, limit each use strictly to the specific criminal offence, delete personal data if authorisation is rejected, document each use in the relevant police file, and submit annual reports on use to relevant market surveillance and national data protection authorities.
exceptions: Authorisation may be sought without undue delay and no later than 48 hours (rather than ex-ante) in certain circumstances.
Authorisation is not required for initial identification of a potential suspect based on objective and verifiable facts directly linked to the offence.
Annual reports may exclude sensitive operational data related to law enforcement.
Reports may be aggregated to cover more than one deployment.
Member States may introduce more restrictive national laws in accordance with Union law.

obligations.summary: Deployers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III that make or assist in making decisions related to natural persons must inform those natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system.
exceptions: Obligation is without prejudice to Article 50.
For high-risk AI systems used for law enforcement purposes, Article 13 of Directive (EU) 2016/680 applies instead.

obligations.summary: Deployers must cooperate with relevant competent authorities in any action those authorities take in relation to the high-risk AI system in order to implement this Regulation.
